body: Microsoft filed suit against JLL on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, in New York County Supreme Court, Bisnow reported on Oct. 12. According to the complaint, JLL was overseeing the build-out of Microsoft's roughly 150,000-square-foot office space at 122 Fifth Ave., a landmarked 11-story building in Manhattan's Flatiron area where Microsoft moved in as anchor tenant in July 2023. Microsoft says JLL was hired in 2012 as project manager for properties Microsoft occupies, as part of a facilities management outsourcing deal Microsoft formally signed with CBRE in 2013. The Bromley Cos. owns the building and redeveloped it in conjunction with Microsoft's arrival, Bisnow reported, citing the New York Post.

The underlying claim dates to March 2023, when a construction worker says he was struck by a forklift at the building and suffered serious, permanent injuries. He sued in Kings County Supreme Court in 2024, naming the building's ownership entity and the contractors, and in June 2025 added Microsoft and the forklift operator as defendants.

Microsoft alleges that its project management agreement required JLL to indemnify it against lawsuits related to the build-out, including attorney fees and damages, and that JLL agreed to add Microsoft as an insured under JLL's $10 million liability policy during the build-out but did not do so. It also claims JLL breached its duty of good faith and fair dealing. According to the complaint, JLL's counsel refused coverage on the grounds that the building's ownership had retained the forklift operator's company and that the worker was on a separate project in the building. Microsoft contends both the worker and the operator were working on Microsoft's space, and calls the denial "factually incorrect" and made without investigation.
JLL and Microsoft did not immediately respond to Bisnow's requests for comment. The $10 million figure is the policy limit Microsoft says it should have been insured under, not a damages demand.

timeline.label: Worker allegedly struck by forklift during build-out at 122 Fifth Avenue
Microsoft moves into the building as anchor tenant
Microsoft added as a defendant in the worker's Kings County personal-injury suit
Microsoft sues JLL in New York County Supreme Court over defense, indemnity and insurance
